messages:
maria_g: Heads-up — AcmePay reported a subtle change in reply length/nuance after the v9.2 model push. They provided side-by-side examples and repro steps.

maria_g: Customer quote: 'Answers feel more clipped and skip the gentle clarifications we relied on. Not outright wrong, just less helpful in edge cases.' :thinking_face:

maria_g: Customer repro (they call our hosted API):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-v9.2",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How do I reconcile a mismatch between ledger A and ledger B for a single invoice?"}],
  "max_tokens": 220,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

maria_g: Before v9.2 (they pasted):
"""
You can start by checking the transaction timestamps and matching invoice IDs across both ledgers. If you still see a mismatch, run a balance reconciliation: 1) export invoice rows, 2) join on invoice_id, 3) identify differing amounts; common causes are partial refunds or posting delays. If you want, I can provide a SQL snippet.
"""

maria_g: After v9.2 (their reported output):
"""
Check timestamps and invoice IDs. If mismatch persists, export and compare rows.
"""

maria_g: They say the new reply removed the offer to provide a SQL snippet and removed softening language like 'you can' / 'if you want'. Customer uses those follow-ups in chat flows so UX regressions matter.

devon_support: Thanks, forwarding to infra + ML. Do we have any canary logs for that rollout window? @redwood-deploy-bot can you confirm which regions got v9.2 and when?

redwood-deploy-bot: v9.2 rolled to hosted-prod in us-east-1 at 2026-02-28T14:02:11Z (canary -> 100% over 45m). No rollback recorded.

kevin_ml: Interesting — sounds like reduced elaboration rather than factual error. Two quick things: 1) Did they change system prompt or default generation params? 2) Any change in token budget/quantization that might trim completions?

maria_g: Customer claims they didn't change prompts or params. They attach sample request headers showing standard account defaults. Attaching convo logs in support ticket (I pasted relevant snippets above).

kevin_ml: Can we repro internally. Steps I'll run: 1) hit v9.1 and v9.2 with identical inputs and params 0/seed, 2) capture top-k/top_p/token usage, 3) diff outputs and token counts, 4) run eval over small prompt set measuring mean response length and presence of followup offers.

jordan_prod: FYI infra reported a single config tweak for v9.2: default max_new_tokens cap enforcement tightened for streaming to prevent runaway token billing. Could that explain shortened replies?

kevin_ml: Possibly — but customer shows full token windows (they allowed 220). Need to verify server-side enforced caps or truncated stream frames. I'll add a check for truncated_content metadata on responses.

maria_g: Customer impact — they have an automated flow that turns model replies into follow-ups. Missing 'would you like the SQL?' breaks the downstream UX. They flagged as P2.

devon_support: Can you share the exact header they send? Also asked if this appears across multiple customers or just AcmePay.

maria_g: Header snip: Authorization: Bearer sk-live-... ; model: redwood-v9.2 ; content-type: application/json. They've run other customers; small number of other accounts reported similar tone tightening after the same deploy (internal support queue has 3 more).

kevin_ml: OK. I'll run the A/B now and post findings. If it's model behavioral drift, plan: 1) fast rollback of model tag for hosted API for a controlled subset OR 2) tweak prompting via system prompt augmentation to re-introduce polite offers.

redwood-deploy-bot: Canary note: v9.2 gradation logs attached: average tokens per response down 6% during canary window compared to baseline.

kevin_ml: That token delta is small but aligns with reported behavior. Could be due to temperature or decoding change in the new model. I'll diff the decode configs and kernel quantization options.

devon_support: Thanks — customer asked for ETA. Any estimate?

kevin_ml: Initial repro + A/B in ~90min. If repro holds, can propose a rollback window in next 2–4 hours.

maria_g: I'll tell AcmePay we're triaging and expect update in ~2 hours. They're happy to share more examples if needed. :thumbsup:

kevin_ml: Quick note — if we can't roll back, short-term mitigation: add a system prompt patch for hosted API that appends a short persona hint: "When appropriate, offer example snippets or follow-up suggestions." That can be pushed immediately to routing layer for affected accounts.

devon_support: Good plan. Keep thread updated with the A/B outputs and token metrics.

kevin_ml: Posting A/B results in 60m.

maria_g: Thanks team.
